title: Adaptive dequantization pipeline and KV-aligned batching windowing for mixed-precision kernels
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Performance: ~15-22% throughput improvement on mixed INT8/FP8 workloads (varies by model and sequence length)
Feature: opt-in runtime flag `dequant.adaptive_pipeline=true` and new batch-window alignment for KV caches
Compatibility: fallbacks to previous dequant path when model geometry or hardware does not support fused kernels
body: Context: customer workloads and internal benchmarks showed inconsistent gains when enabling INT8/FP8 smoothquant paths alongside continuous batching and the KV cache. Two problems were apparent: (1) naive dequant->compute->requant ordering incurred extra per-token copies when requests in the same batch had different effective key/value prefix lengths, and (2) per-head scale mismatches in mixed-precision kernels produced small but measurable accuracy drift at tail latencies. Motivation: we need a single, production-safe change that improves end-to-end token throughput while preserving numeric fidelity and making the fused kernels robust to variable KV alignment and continuous batching semantics. Summary of changes: introduced an adaptive dequantization pipeline that defers full dequant work until per-batch KV alignment is known; implemented a batch-window coalescer that groups inflight requests into short windows (configurable default 4ms) to enable wider batching without violating latency SLOs; added a per-head scale correction step in the fused int8/fp8 kernels that compensates for quantization split across attention heads; changed kernel registration to prefer aligned fused kernels when a KV-alignment hint is present; added a runtime toggle `dequant.adaptive_pipeline` with three modes (off, conservative, adaptive). Performance: in production-like harnesses (GPT-2 XL / seq_len=1024, 8-GPU V100 cluster), adaptive mode shows median throughput +18% and p95 latency change within +3ms across steady-state traffic; single-GPU local perf tests for smaller models (LLaMA-7B) show +12% throughput and no regression in perplexity on standard eval sets. Correctness: we added deterministic unit tests that exercise misaligned KV scenarios and a regression suite validating output logits against baseline fp32 within epsilon=1e-3 for classification tasks. Rollout plan: flag gated behind `dequant.adaptive_pipeline` disabled by default; staged rollout to dedicated clusters for one week, then gradual Hosted rollout with canary percent increases; automatic fallback to legacy dequant path if error rates increase >0.5% or numeric regressions exceed threshold. Backwards compatibility: this change does not require model changes; it is safe for customers pinned to older model versions. Caveats: the adaptive pipeline adds a small CPU scheduling overhead (measured ~0.3ms per batch window), so for ultra-low-latency single-token workloads customers should keep the flag off. Notes: references to internal experiments and ticket INT-912 included.
